page: Microsoft Azure D4nls_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance within the network-optimized, low-memory Dnlv6 series. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The compute topology features four dedicated vCPUs mapped across two physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 acceleration, and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include integrated local storage or discrete graphics processing units, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent block devices. Benchmark evaluations show balanced performance in compute-focused single-threaded scenarios, with stress-ng single-core execution scoring 1620.58 and PassMark CPU encryption reaching 3525.36. Memory-intensive and parallel metrics remain in lower tiers, recording 32.72 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 24.09 GB/sec write bandwidth, and 3312.48 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Web-tier throughput registers at 6.5 GB/sec, while small model text generation processes 152.95 tokens per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the D4nls_v6 provides an economical allocation of memory for applications where larger RAM-to-vCPU footprints are unnecessary. The reduced memory ratio provides efficient resource utilization for processing tasks that primarily demand clock frequency and network capability rather than in-memory working sets. Workloads suitable for this profile include front-end web serving, microservices routing, proxy handling, and standard stateless compute tasks operating against external databases or remote storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4nls_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 8.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptographic instruction sets, while local storage and dedicated GPUs are absent, requiring reliance on remote storage. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core capabilities, achieving 1620.58 in stress-ng single-core tests, 6.5 GB/sec in static web throughput, and 3525.36 in encryption processing, though multi-threaded execution and raw memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles. The hardware architecture and resource density make the D4nls_v6 suitable for lightweight compute pipelines, network proxies, microservices, and stateless web application serving.
